newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends steady with US after range trading.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends steady with US after range trading.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended steady on Tuesday having failed to break out of a narrow trading range.
March Brent closed just one cent up at $21.14 a barrel, off a low of $21.05 and a session high of $21.38.
"(Brent) had no will of its own today it was stuck in a range and just following (NYMEX crude)," said one dealer.
March NYMEX crude also ended fairly steady at $22.40 a barrel after failing to sustain an early upside break and then bouncing off support at $22.25.
Brent breached light support at $21.20 a barrel as it came off highs and brokers said that the next support level was at $21.00 and Monday's low of $20.55.
Brokers said that the market shrugged off a nationwide workers strike in oil-producing Colombia that started at midnight on Monday.
"We certainly didn't pick up any bullishness in the States over that," said one.
Earlier, prompt IPE gas oil closed strongly ahead of its expiry tomorrow, widening the front month backwardation to almost $10 a tonne.
The Feb contract closed up $4.25 a tonne at $192.50, off a session high of $194. The March contract gained just $1.50 a tonne, however, to close at $182.75.
"It looks like the longs are giving it a bit of a squeeze," said one dealer.
Brokers expected a fairly large physical delivery into the screen of 600,000 to 700,000 tonnes, with some 300,000 tonnes expected to be delivered to one trading house alone.
Open interest at the close of trade on Tuesday was 13,072 lots, or 1,307,200 tonnes.

Oil markets on both sides of the Atlantic were waiting for direction from weekly U.S. oil stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), due to be released after the close of trade on Tuesday.
But the APIs were not expected to throw up any great surprises.

"Crude looks moderately flat, gasoline should rise for seasonal reasons and distillates should draw down due to winter demand," brokers GNI said in their daily report. "However, note the distillate draw at the same last year was quite dramatic so we're likely to see a larger surplus compared to year ago."
Dealers were expecting a draw on distillate stocks of 1.5 to 3.5 million barrels, with inventories to hold above year-ago levels for the second consecutive week.
Gasoline stocks were seen increasing 1.4 to four million barrels, while crude stocks were seen rising by two million barrels.
